test_title: PYST 32: SSC GD Constable 2025 - English (Held On: 19 Feb, 2025 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Select the sentence with an error in the adverb used.

options.text: He answered the questions surprisingly well during the interview.
She performs her duties more diligently than anyone else in the team.
The students completed the assignment less thorough than expected.
The new software runs more efficiently than the previous version.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the adverb "less thorough" in Option 3.
 
• The correct adverbial form should be "less thoroughly" because it modifies the verb "completed" and refers to the manner of completing the assignment.
 
• Adverbs are typically used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, and they often end in "-ly" when describing the manner of an action.
 
• Thus, the correct sentence should be: "The students completed the assignment less thoroughly than expected."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The students completed the assignment less thoroughly than expected."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "He answered the questions surprisingly well during the interview." – This sentence is correct as the adverb "surprisingly well" is used appropriately to describe how the questions were answered.
 
• **Option 2:** "She performs her duties more diligently than anyone else in the team." – This sentence is correct as the adverb "more diligently" properly modifies the verb "performs."
 
• **Option 4:** "The new software runs more efficiently than the previous version." – This sentence is correct as the adverb "more efficiently" is used correctly to describe how the software runs.
